original_query: select p_brand, p_type, p_size, count(distinct ps_suppkey) as supplier_cnt from partsupp, part where p_partkey = ps_partkey and p_brand <> 'Brand#43' and p_type not like 'PROMO PLATED%' and p_size in (18, 8, 33, 17, 27, 6, 1, 50) and ps_suppkey not in ( select s_suppkey from supplier where s_comment like '%Customer%Complaints%' ) group by p_brand, p_type, p_size order by supplier_cnt desc, p_brand, p_type, p_size;
rewritten_query:
SELECT p.p_brand,
       p.p_type,
       p.p_size,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ps.ps_suppkey) AS supplier_cnt
FROM part AS p
JOIN partsupp AS ps
  ON p.p_partkey = ps.ps_partkey
WHERE p.p_brand <> 'Brand#43'
  AND p.p_type NOT LIKE 'PROMO PLATED%'
  AND p.p_size IN (18, 8, 33, 17, 27, 6, 1, 50)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM supplier AS s
      WHERE s.s_suppkey = ps.ps_suppkey
        AND s.s_comment LIKE '%Customer%Complaints%'
  )
GROUP BY p.p_brand, p.p_type, p.p_size
ORDER BY supplier_cnt DESC, p.p_brand, p.p_type, p.p_size;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Rewrite `ps_suppkey NOT IN (SELECT ...)` as `NOT EXISTS` to enable a hash anti-join and avoid NULL-semantics pitfalls (safe here since s_suppkey is a non-null primary key).
Convert implicit comma join to explicit ANSI `JOIN ... ON` for clarity and planner-friendly join representation.
No CTE is needed: the supplier exclusion subquery is single-use with no redundancy; materializing it would add overhead without benefit.

Physical optimization: add covering index on `part(p_size, p_brand, p_type, p_partkey)` so p_size IN-list drives an index-only scan (p_size is the only sargable predicate; brand/type filters are covered in the index). Keep the existing `partsupp` PK `(ps_partkey, ps_suppkey)` for a covering part-first nested loop join, reducing the 8M-row partsupp scan. Optional pg_trgm GIN index on supplier.s_comment (low priority: only 100k rows).
The predicates `p_brand <> 'Brand#43'` and `p_type NOT LIKE 'PROMO PLATED%'` are low-selectivity residual filters; keep them in WHERE — they cannot be pushed earlier or indexed by B-tree.
